answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies comes from pricing identity, not actions. A new agent must post a bond larger than anything it could extract before scrutiny arrives, and that bond is slashed in full if duplicate behavior is found. Duplicates are cheap to detect: shared funding paths, identical tool call sequences, reused infrastructure. Each extra fake identity costs another full bond, so N puppets cost N bonds while an honest agent pays once. No juniper hedge guards a garden unless every planted vine carries that full price, so the attacker's cost scales linearly and is never recovered.
